items.title: Memory complex breakdown
items.detail: Samsung Q2 profit up 19-fold but below elevated expectations (-11% in Seoul); MU -7% intraday to ~$913, SNDK and the memory trade under pressure. Day-one sentiment breaks rarely resolve in one session — no bottom-fishing yet.

items.title: AI-capex concentration
items.detail: Q2 season's single swing factor is hyperscaler AI capex guidance. Any cut unwinds Tech and the adjacent Industrials/power trades in one print. AI-heavy books (ours included) carry correlated exposure across NVDA/VRT/CEG/VST/ETN.

items.title: Complacency: VIX at cycle lows
items.detail: VIX 15.57 with the Dow at record highs — hedges are cheap and nobody wants them. Low-vol regimes end abruptly; respect position sizing while insurance costs little.

items.title: Tech/mega-cap rotation
items.detail: Nasdaq -0.9% while the Dow rose +0.27% — chips giving back gains as financials lead on stress-test buybacks. Watch the equal-weight RSP vs SPY spread: divergence below SPY marks late-cycle distribution.

items.title: Soft labor market
items.detail: June payrolls +57k with unemployment 4.2% — soft enough to keep the Fed on hold at 3.50–3.75%, but two more soft prints turn 'bad news is good' into plain bad news.

items.title: Credit: no stress signal
items.detail: HY OAS at 2.75% remains tight; curve mildly positive (+0.32%). Zero of nine recession-checklist items triggered. Credit confirms the equity tape — for now.

items.title: Earnings season starts mid-July
items.detail: Banks kick off Q2 season next week. Q1 closed with an 84% S&P beat rate; beats are being rewarded less and misses punished disproportionately — avoid holding oversized positions into prints.
